video.title: How He Turned a Small Cleaning Side Hustle Into a Nationwide Company

summary: Dalton Dry describes starting Clean Bro as a residential cleaning side business while working full time, then growing it with help from systems, staff and customer acquisition. The business expanded into CB Facility Services, which wins commercial and government cleaning work across multiple US states through outbound email and vendor portals. Dalton describes revenue, contract and advertising results, but also early losses, poor lead-generation contracts and demanding overnight operations. His main operating principle is to hire capable people and build the company so he does not have to deliver the service himself.

ideas.delivery: Cleaners perform the home cleans. Dalton initially handled some weekend and evening cleans, including resolving complaints, but later stopped selling and booking individual cleans. A VA handles residential sales; staff and systems run the operation.
unit_economics_claims: Dalton reported about $10,000 in booked revenue per month attributed to the residential VA in each of the previous three months.
He reported about $4,500 in monthly ad spend and about 30% residential margins after ad spend and labour.
He reported an 8x return on Facebook ad spend and 2x returns on Thumbtack and Angi.
tools: CRM or business-management platform, name not stated
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Dalton says he filed for an LLC, called around, created his first customer and booked his first clean within 24 hours; he does not state when the first payment arrived.

acquisition.how: SEO, paid ads and marketplace leads can be managed by software and agents with routine checks. Local referrals and Facebook group posting still need human judgment. In the UK, avoid unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals without consent.

onboarding.how: A VA can handle warm lead calls and booking with scripts and scheduling software; unusual requests and complaints need human review.

delivery.how: People must physically clean homes and bring or use supplies.

billing.how: Recurring invoices and payment reminders could be automated, with a person reviewing exceptions; the transcript does not describe their billing process.

support.how: A person handles customer concerns. Dalton says he prefers human conversations because customers want empathy.

uk_applicability.notes: Residential cleaning demand and service delivery translate to the UK. Local labour, insurance, consumer terms and pricing would need UK-specific setup.

risks: Dalton says the business initially spent everything it made and was not profitable.
Lead-generation contracts can lock the business into a long term without producing useful leads.
Facebook group posting was manual and felt like a race to the bottom on price.
Paid leads can be expensive; reported margins were about 30% after ad spend and labour.
The service depends on reliable cleaners, and Dalton describes no-shows and stolen equipment.
In the UK, unsolicited marketing messages to individuals and sole traders require consent under PECR; cold outreach to limited companies still needs compliant targeting and opt-out handling.

ideas.name: CB Facility Services commercial cleaning
ideas.one_liner: A commercial janitorial company that wins multi-site contracts through outbound prospecting, bids and supplier portals, then staffs local cleaners.
ideas.business_model: Commercial cleaning contracts, including recurring monthly contracts and project work.
ideas.customer: Commercial facilities companies, retail chains, banks, universities and government or municipal buyers.
ideas.problem: Organizations need cleaning across buildings and locations, and need contractors who can staff and manage the work reliably.
ideas.offer: Commercial janitorial cleaning for banks, retail sites, student dorms and municipal buildings. Specific service specifications are not stated.

pricing.model: Contract pricing; at least one contract was described as monthly, while bid pricing is calculated using a company matrix.

price_points.label: Contract value after initial work expanded

pricing.notes: Dalton first describes a $20,000 per month contract, then says the initial contract was not that large but reached about $22,000 per month after additional bank work. He does not give rates per building or bid.

acquisition_channels.details: Commercial prospects found the company after HSA helped build the website and improve its Google presence; a commercial company approached them for a quote.

quote.text: they reached out to us proactively because we had at that point established some SEO
quote.speaker: Dalton Dry

acquisition_channels.details: Dalton says the South Carolina retail contract came from cold email. The company runs outbound email campaigns from about 20 CB Facility Services inboxes and sends tens of thousands of emails per month.

quote.text: I have about I think 20 total um CB facility services inboxes that are all doing outbound campaigns all day
quote.speaker: Dalton Dry

acquisition_channels.details: The company applies through vendor portals on large corporate facilities companies' websites, then bids on opportunities when invited.

quote.text: I could just go to their website, go apply to be a vendor, and if they have an opportunity and our company looks and has some legitimacy to it, they'll reach out
quote.speaker: Dalton Dry

acquisition_channels.details: A staff bidder scouts federal and local municipality opportunities, applies through vendor portals and submits bids. Dalton also describes registering to become a federal contractor and a state vendor.

quote.text: one of my staff, he's a full-time bidder, and all he does is scout the country for these federal bids and these local municipality bids
quote.speaker: Dalton Dry

acquisition_channels.details: The operations manager searches Facebook groups for small cleaning businesses to recruit as local delivery partners.

quote.text: So we we'll go to Facebook groups. We'll look for folks to advertise their small cleaning businesses.
quote.speaker: Dalton Dry

ideas.delivery: Dalton and staff quote and manage contracts remotely. They recruit local cleaners or small cleaning businesses, interview and vet them, and have them perform the cleaning and bring supplies; the company provides chemicals. A US-based operations manager manages operations. Dalton sometimes visits a site at launch, while cleaners handle recurring physical work. Early bank jobs required night shifts, access codes, equipment and supply coordination, and regular client updates.
unit_economics_claims: Dalton says the first commercial contract reached about $22,000 per month after the initial bank rollout expanded.
The bank rollout grew to 82 locations within 30 days.
Another rollout included 42 retail clothing locations in South Carolina.
The Penn State dorm project was expected to use about 20 cleaners to clean about 600 dorms.
Dalton says the business sends tens of thousands of outbound emails per month.
tools: Email inboxes and outbound campaign software, names not stated
Federal, state and corporate vendor portals
ideas.startup_cost: Not stated. Dalton says insurance costs and required coverage increased for bank work, but gives no amounts.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: The first commercial company approached them after the business had established SEO; Dalton says the contract reached about $22,000 per month after initial jobs expanded. Exact time from launch to first payment is not stated.

acquisition.how: Agents can research corporate accounts, monitor vendor portals and draft bids or cold emails, with people approving eligibility, pricing and submissions. UK cold email rules differ by recipient type: unsolicited email to limited companies can be permissible, while sole traders and individuals generally require consent under PECR.

onboarding.how: Agents can collect documents and track onboarding, but interviews, vetting, background checks and site-specific access coordination require human oversight.

delivery.how: Cleaners must physically clean sites, restock or use supplies, and resolve access problems.

billing.how: Contract billing and invoice reminders could be automated from schedules and approved work records; the transcript does not state the billing system.

support.how: A manager must coordinate cleaners, access, supplies and client updates, especially when work fails overnight.

uk_applicability.notes: Commercial cleaning contracts and facilities procurement exist in the UK, but procurement rules, public-sector tender portals, insurance, employment and contractor requirements differ. The US federal and state contracting process described would need to be replaced with UK routes. Cold email must follow UK PECR rules based on recipient type.

risks: The first bank rollout created overnight operational work for Dalton and his wife, including calls until 2–4 a.m. when access codes, keys or supplies failed.
The company encountered cleaners who no-showed or stole equipment; hiring and trust are essential to remote delivery.
Commercial work requires higher insurance coverage, background checks and formal processes.
Large multi-site contracts can expand faster than staffing and operations capacity.
Bids require accurate costs and pricing; Dalton says he initially did not know how to price commercial work.
In the UK, unsolicited marketing email to individuals and sole traders generally requires consent under PECR; cold outreach to corporate subscribers needs appropriate compliance and opt-out handling.

tactics.name: Start with a simple first clean

tactics.name: Build inbound demand before relying on lead scraping
steps: Create a website early.
Improve the site's SEO and Google presence so local customers can find the company.
Track which channels generate leads and reduce reliance on manual group posting when it consumes too much time.

tactics.name: Test lead channels and monitor their return
steps: Test paid social and marketplace leads rather than assuming one channel works in every market.
Track booked revenue and ad spend by channel.
Keep using channels that return enough revenue to cover labour and acquisition costs; review margins as recurring work builds.

quote.text: our return um on uh ad spend for Facebook um is is our our has been our best
quote.speaker: Dalton Dry

tactics.name: Train a VA to handle warm residential sales
steps: Recruit and vet candidates carefully.
Have the VA attend the company's sales calls and receive training.
Transfer routine warm-lead calls and booking to the VA, then monitor booked revenue.

tactics.name: Use service performance and communication to expand a commercial account
steps: Quote the initial sites carefully and establish who handles access, keys, supplies and escalation.
Prioritize reliable cleaning and proactive communication with the client's lead.
Record failures and clearly report what broke and what needs attention.
Use consistent delivery to earn additional sites from the same chain.

steps: Register as a federal contractor or as a vendor with the relevant state or corporate buyer.

steps: Review a large candidate pool and interview a smaller shortlist.

Keep replacing manual work with better processes and capable people.

evidence_quality.rationale: Dalton is a first-hand operator and gives specific channels, hiring practices, contract examples and operating problems. Several results are self-reported, definitions of revenue and return on ad spend are not fully explained, and the transcript contains apparent transcription errors and some ambiguous figures.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: The hosts promote Home Service Academy, which Dalton joined and credits with coaching and help improving the website and SEO. The episode includes a host-read sales pitch for HSA.
